title: Repeating decimals to fractions
competency: Convert a repeating decimal to a fraction in simplest form.

keywords.def: A decimal in which a block of digits repeats for ever, such as 0.333… or 0.2323…
A line over the repeating digits of a decimal: 0.3̅ means 0.333…
A number that can be written a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0.

en.text: Call the decimal d. Multiply d by a power of 10 so the repeating part lines up. Subtract to remove the repeating part. Then solve for d. For 0.555…, 10d = 5.555…, so 9d = 5 and d = 5/9. Every repeating decimal is a rational number.

am.text: አስርዮሹን d በለው። የሚደጋገመው ክፍል እንዲሰለፍ dን በ10 ኃይል አባዛ። የሚደጋገመውን ክፍል ለማስወገድ ቀንስ። ከዚያ dን ፈልግ። ለ0.555…፣ 10d = 5.555… ስለሆነ 9d = 5 እና d = 5/9። እያንዳንዱ ተደጋጋሚ አስርዮሽ ምክንያታዊ ቁጥር ነው።

screens.title: Which fraction is 0.555…?
screens.text: In 1.2.1 you saw that dividing gives decimals like 0.555… Now go the other way.
screens.ask: Which fraction do you think equals 0.555…?
screens.after:
5/10 = 0.5 and 1/2 = 0.5: they stop.
5/99 = 0.0505…: the block 05 repeats.
5/9 = 0.555…: only the 5 repeats. That is the one.
Read the method to see how to find it without guessing.

screens.title: Line up, then subtract
paras: Multiply the decimal by a power of 10. Choose it so the repeating part lines up.
Then subtract to remove the repeating part.
What is left is a simple equation. Solve it for d.

screens.title: Name it
defs: A decimal where a block of digits repeats for ever. Every repeating decimal can be written as a fraction, so it is rational.

screens.title: Which power of 10?
screens.text: Repeating decimal to fraction: to convert 0.4̅7̅ to a fraction, you first multiply d by:
screens.why:
Count the digits under the bar: 4 and 7, so two digits repeat.
Multiply by 10² = 100: 100d = 47.4̅7̅.
Now 100d and d have the same tail .4̅7̅.
Subtracting removes the tail: 99d = 47.
(10d = 4.7̅4̅ has a different tail, so it does not line up.)
screens.clue: Count the digits under the bar.

screens.text: The repeating part starts right after the point.
steps: (a) Let d = 0.5̅. One digit repeats, so multiply by 10: 10d = 5.5̅.
(b) Let d = 2.1̅2̅. Two digits repeat, so 100d = 212.1̅2̅.

screens.title: Try one
screens.text: Repeating decimal to fraction: what fraction is 0.4̅?
screens.why:
Let d = 0.4̅ = 0.444…
One digit repeats, so 10d = 4.444…
Subtract: 10d − d = 4.444… − 0.444… = 4. So 9d = 4.
Divide by 9: d = 4/9.
Check: 4 ÷ 9 = 0.444… (4/10 = 0.4 stops.)
screens.clue: Follow Example 1(a) with 4 in place of 5.

screens.title: When the repeat starts later
paras: Sometimes a digit comes before the repeating block, as in 0.1222…
Then make two numbers that both line up.
Multiply so the point sits just before the first repeat. Multiply again so it sits after one full block.
screens.note: Correction: in Example 2(a) the printed book divides 90d = 11 "by 99" and gives d = 11/99. Dividing by 90 gives d = 11/90. Check: 11 ÷ 90 = 0.1222…, while 11/99 = 0.1111…

screens.text: One digit sits before the repeating block.

screens.title: Two repeating digits
screens.ask: Two repeating digits to a fraction: 0.1̅4̅ = ___ as a fraction.
screens.why:
Let d = 0.1̅4̅. Two digits repeat, so 100d = 14.1̅4̅.
Subtract: 100d − d = 14.1̅4̅ − 0.1̅4̅ = 14.
So 99d = 14.
Divide by 99: d = 14/99.
screens.clue: Subtract d from 100d. What is left?

screens.title: Check the book
screens.why:
Let d = 0.1222… Then 100d = 12.2̅ and 10d = 1.2̅.
Subtract: 90d = 11, so d = 11/90.
But 11/99 = 0.1111…, not 0.1222…
So 0.12̅ = 11/90, and the statement is false.
screens.clue: Divide 11 by 99 on your calculator. Does it give 0.1222…?

screens.title: Sharing coffee beans
screens.text: A trader in Jimma says each bag holds 2.6̅ kg of coffee beans. That is 2.666… kg.
screens.ask: Repeating decimal to fraction in simplest form: each bag holds ___ kg.
screens.why:
Let d = 2.6̅ = 2.666…
One digit repeats, so 10d = 26.666…
Subtract: 10d − d = 24, so 9d = 24.
d = 24/9. GCF(24, 9) = 3, so d = 8/3.
Check: 8 ÷ 3 = 2.666… kg.
screens.clue: One digit repeats. Multiply d by 10, then subtract d.
screens.worked: Let d = 2.6̅. Then 10d = 26.6̅. Subtract: 9d = 24. So d = 24/9 = 8/3 kg.

screens.title: Put the steps in order: 0.4̅7̅ as a fraction
screens.why:
First name the decimal: d = 0.4̅7̅.
Two digits repeat, so multiply by 100 to line up the tails.
Subtract d to remove the tail: 99d = 47.
Divide by 99: d = 47/99.
screens.clue: Name the decimal first. Divide only at the very end.

screens.title: Match each repeating decimal to its fraction
screens.clue: Count the digits under the bar. Is there a digit before the repeat?

items.why:
Let d = 2.6̅. One digit repeats, so 10d = 26.6̅.
Subtract: 10d − d = 26.6̅ − 2.6̅ = 24.
So 9d = 24 and d = 24/9.
Simplify by 3: d = 8/3 = 2⅔.

Let d = 0.1̅4̅. Two digits repeat, so 100d = 14.1̅4̅.
Subtract: 100d − d = 14.
So 99d = 14 and d = 14/99.
GCF(14, 99) = 1, so this is the simplest form.

Let d = 0.71616… The 7 comes before the repeating block 16.
10d = 7.1̅6̅ (the point sits just before the block).
1000d = 716.1̅6̅ (one full block later).
Subtract: 1000d − 10d = 716 − 7 = 709. So 990d = 709.
d = 709/990.

The bar is over the 1 and 2 after 1.32, so d = 1.32121212…
The digits 1.3 come before the repeat. 100d = 132.1̅2̅ puts the point just before a block.
10000d = 13212.1̅2̅ is one block (two digits) later.
Subtract: 9900d = 13212 − 132 = 13080.
d = 13080/9900 = 218/165 (divide both by 60).

items.clue: Work with 0.532̅1̅3̅ first. Use 100000d and 100d. Put the minus sign back at the end.

test.ask: Repeating decimal to fraction: 0.7̅ = ___ as a fraction.

test.text: Repeating decimal to fraction: to convert 0.12̅ to a fraction, which two multiples of d line up?
test.why:
d = 0.1222… The 1 comes before the repeating 2.
10d = 1.222… puts the point just before the repeat.
100d = 12.222… puts it one block later.
Both end in 2̅, so 100d − 10d = 11 has no tail.
So use 100d and 10d.

Let d = 2.1212… Two digits repeat, so 100d = 212.1212…
Subtract: 100d − d = 210, so 99d = 210.
d = 210/99. GCF(210, 99) = 3, so d = 70/33.
True.

notes.text: In Example 2(a) the printed book divides 90d = 11 "by 99" and gives d = 11/99. Dividing by 90 gives d = 11/90. Check: 11 ÷ 90 = 0.1222…, while 11/99 = 0.1111…

screens.title: Read a bar
screens.text: A bar sits over the digits that repeat for ever.
steps: Count the digits under the bar. That tells you the length of the repeating block.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.why:
The bar covers both the 4 and the 7.
So the block 47 repeats for ever.
0.4̅7̅ = 0.474747…
(0.4777… would be written 0.47̅, with the bar over the 7 only.)
screens.clue: Which digits are under the bar?
